newsitem.title: ANGOLA: UNITA cancels Kabila speech to Angolan assembly.
newsitem.headline: UNITA cancels Kabila speech to Angolan assembly.

text.p: UNITA deputies have cancelled a meeting of Angola's national assembly that was to have been addressed by Congolese President Laurent Kabila, an official of the former rebel movement said on Wednesday.
"It would be unconstitutional for an elected parliament to meet for an unelected president," said Abe Chivukuvuku, UNITA's leader in the national assembly.
Chivukuvuku said only a permanent parliamentary standing committee had the constitutional authority to call such meetings and the committee had not met.

The former rebels are a minority party with 70 seats in the national assembly that they took up earlier this year as part of a three-year-old peace process that ended two decades of civil war against the ruling MPLA party.
Kabila, who arrived in Angola on Tuesday, will still meet a small group of deputies in the assembly building before returning home to Kinshasa later on Wednesday, said Chivukuvuku.

Diplomats and officials close to Angola's long peace process say Kabila and Angolan President Eduardo dos Santos may discuss security issues involving the former UNITA rebels, who still control large areas of the Angolan countryside.

Military tension has mounted ahead of a mid-August deadline for UNITA to comply with a number of U.N. Security Council demands. Diplomats and officials have expressed fears that the country is drifting towards renewed conflict.
The Angolan government has been suspected of supporting Kabila's drive to depose former Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko, a longtime UNITA ally, whose government fell to Kabila's rebels in May.
Diplomats and officials close to the Angolan peace process say the two presidents are exploring ways to cooperate in defeating UNITA in the event of a renewal of hostilities.
